results: 1. Comprehensive ophthalmic examination with visual acuity, pupils, ocular motility, and slit-lamp examination
ocular motility examination: full in all directions
pupil examination (size, light reaction): equal and reactive
visual acuity and colour vision: normal
2. Bilateral eyelid measurements, including marginal reflex distance 1, palpebral fissure height, levator function, and eyelid crease height
lid position and measurement (MRD1 both sides): MRD1 raised on the LEFT (retraction); right lid height normal - the right eye is NOT ptotic
3. Manual elevation of the apparently ptotic eyelid to assess for contralateral eyelid descent
4. Assessment of eyelid position in downgaze and upgaze
5. Review of prior photographs and operative records
surgical history: closed-approach structural rhinoplasty; retraction noted on postoperative day 6
6. Orbital and eyelid examination for masses, scarring, and levator dysfunction
pain and periorbital inspection: no lagophthalmos and no corneal erosion
7. Thyroid-stimulating hormone and free thyroxine blood tests
8. Orbital MRI with contrast and dedicated eyelid imaging
MRI orbits: no extraocular muscle enlargement, no mass
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Acquired isolated left upper-eyelid retraction caused by postoperative levator/Müller muscle dysfunction following closed structural rhinoplasty (non-thyroidal postoperative eyelid retraction)

Alternative: Idiopathic unilateral upper-eyelid retraction

Alternative: Subclinical contralateral eyelid ptosis causing apparent left eyelid retraction

Alternative: Postoperative orbital or eyelid scarring causing mechanical upper-eyelid retraction
